chapter: Touring abroad and the future of music
title: Summer festival plans and jazz education in Europe
summary: He plans Nice and a seven-hall Dutch festival, and says European jazz education is far behind the US but improving.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: I see. What about your festival scene, though? You're going to so many.

Well, we're planning again this next summer to go to -- first to the South of France, to Nice, to that festival. And then on to -- they have a festival now in Holland which lasts three days, and in the same complex -- they have seven halls and seven different performances.
And they soon find out who's drawing and who isn't right?
Wasn't that -- is that the same location that you were involved with a year or two ago, in the summer, with a lot of jazz education activity?
No, I never did this one.
No, I never did this one.
Weren't you in Holland for something like that?
Was supposed to be, and it was cancelled.
Oh, I see. I see. What's your observation about that part of education over there in Europe? Are they --

Well, they're far behind us, but they're doing very well by their standards, and by our standards. But they're much further ahead than we were 20 years ago, and much further behind us in this day and age. So they're making definite progress. I'm very pleased about that. (unintelligible) views to find out what they'd like to play and be a part of.
